import_timing_scope: Continuous parent monotonic interval before first CLI import through initial required query group assertions. Includes process launch, post-stage stats observations and count validation; only collection4 vector/text and collection0 target paths, not all ten index-ready.
multicollection_observation_scope: Each product stage and each stats observation runs in its own measured process. macOS time -l maxrss is that process lifetime peak; inner operation timers have narrower boundaries. 100ms disk samples are observed lower bounds on peaks.
largefile_timing_scope: Monotonic case and worker wall time. First reader verify/open excluded from compact trigger time but included in case total. RSS from /usr/bin/time per supervised process family, not runtime ledger or per-phase peak.
outstanding_measurement_limits: Directory samples are non-atomic sums of sequential stats, not guaranteed simultaneous total/strict peak lower bounds. Original fields preserved; mapped values are sampled maxima only.
Recovery worker per-phase extra logical disk peak was not sampled in original four-case evidence; cannot derive it from final temporary lengths.
Physical read/write bytes and exclusive physical extents of old-reader-retained files are unknown.
No OS cache eviction; first query group is application/process-cold only.
These scale/resource measurements are macOS ARM64 native Rust1.97.1/APFS only; physical Linux full tests are a distinct evidence layer.
No one reader was held across the complete multicollection workflow; existing dedicated per-phase and four crash retained-reader tests retain their own scope.
